sentences.text:
Chintakunta Srinivas Reddy, vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh,
on 12 January, 2024
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice Venkateswarlu Nimmagadda
 Writ Petition No.45056 of 2018
Order:

entities.text: Chintakunta Srinivas Reddy, vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The present writ petition is filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India seeking the following relief:
"...to issue a Writ or Order or Direction more particularly one in the nature of Writ of Mandamus declaring the action of the respondents herein in taking steps to dispossess the petitioner from his lands admeasuring Ac.4.99 cents covered by Sy.No.774 situated at Kummarapalli of Bandapalle Village, Ramapuram Mandal,
Kadapa District, under the guise of laying road to Nadigaddapalli village without following due process of law as illegal, arbitrary and violation of Articles 14, 19, 21 and 300-A of the Constitution of India and consequently direct the respondents not to dispossess from his lands admeasuring Ac.4.99 cents covered by Sy.No.774 situated at Kummarapalli of Bandapalle Village, Ramapuram Mandal, Kadapa District under the guise of laying road to Nadigaddapalli village without following due process of law and to pass".

2. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned Government Pleader for Panchayat Raj and Rural Development appearing for the respondent Nos.1 to 6 and learned Standing Counsel for the 7th respondent.
3.
The contentions of the learned counsel for petitioner is that the respondents are trying to lay road from his land in Sy.No.774 of Nadigaddapalli village.

While laying road they proposed to dispossess the petitioner from the part of land in Sy.No.774 to an extent of Ac.4.99 cents, without adhering to the principles of natural justice and due process as contemplated under Act 30 of 2013 "The Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act,
2013" (for short, Act).

entities.text:
Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act,
2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 4. On the other hand, learned Standing Counsel for the 7th respondent submitted his written instructions dated 06.01.2024, wherein it is categorically admitted that there is no such proposals with the Gram Panchayat for laying any road, more particularly as alleged by the petitioner.

Therefore, in view of the categorical admission on the part of the respondent/Gram Panchayat, it is clear that it is only an apprehension of the petitioner that he may be dispossessed from the part of his subject land.

5. Having regard to the submission made by learned counsel for the petitioner as well as the learned Government Pleader for respondent Nos.1 to 6 and learned Standing Counsel for the 7th respondent Chintakunta Srinivas Reddy, vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh, on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157621116/
1 and on perusal of the material placed on record, this Court is of the considered view that the present Writ Petition is disposed of directing the respondents not to interfere with the peaceful possession and enjoyment of the subject property of the petitioner without adhering the principles of natural justice and due procedure as contemplated under the Act 30 of 2013.

entities.text: Chintakunta Srinivas Reddy, vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Consequently, Miscellaneous Petitions, if any, pending in the Writ Petition shall stand closed.
